issues.description: A 1x1 tracking pixel in the page footer has no text alternative. [SYSTEMIC PATTERN] Tracking pixels are commonly decorative and should be hidden from assistive technology globally.
issues.suggestion: If the image is decorative, add alt="". If it conveys information, add a short, meaningful description.
issues.description_technical: The element is missing the alt attribute, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A blind user relying on a screen reader hears the filename or 'image' and loses any information this image might convey.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers expose the alt attribute as the accessible name of the img element; without it, the AT announces the filename or 'image', providing no semantic value. NVDA + Firefox: announces 'graphic https://dequeuniversity.com/assets/demo-sites/mars/js/seg' as a one-pixel element.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="" to the tracking pixel if it is purely decorative, or alt="<descriptive text>" if it conveys information.

issues.description: A meaningful promotional image in the main content area has no text alternative, so its content is invisible to screen-reader users.
issues.suggestion: Add a concise description of the image's content and purpose.
issues.description_technical: The element is missing the alt attribute, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A blind user cannot know what the image shows or what promotion it represents.
issues.why_technical: Without an alt attribute, screen readers announce the filename or 'image', failing to convey the image's purpose or content. JAWS 2024: announces 'graphic mars-spaceman.jpg' with no context.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="" to the element, e.g., alt="Astronaut floating near Mars surface for Crater Adventure promotion".

issues.description: The image alt text is a filename, which does not describe the image's content or purpose.
issues.suggestion: Replace the filename with a meaningful description of the image.
issues.description_technical: The alt attribute equals a filename, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user hears 'icecream.jpg' instead of a meaningful description of the space station image.
issues.why_technical: Filename-based alt text provides no semantic value and fails to convey the image's meaning to assistive technology users. NVDA + Chrome: announces 'graphic icecream.jpg' which is unrelated to the space station visual.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change alt="icecream.jpg " to alt="International space station orbiting Earth" or similar descriptive text.

issues.description: A channel logo image in the video information area uses generic alt text that does not identify the channel or image content.
issues.suggestion: Use the channel name or a meaningful description as the alt text.
issues.description_technical: The alt attribute is generic ('thumbnail-image'), violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user cannot identify which channel or logo this image represents.
issues.why_technical: Generic alt text does not provide an accessible name that conveys the image's purpose or content to assistive technology. VoiceOver iOS: announces 'thumbnail image' without identifying the channel.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change alt="thumbnail-image" to alt="<Channel Name> channel logo" or similar descriptive text.

issues.element: <svg height="100%" version="1.1" viewbox="0 0 36 36" width="100%"><!-- SVG desenho omitido --></svg>
issues.description: An SVG icon has no accessible name and is not marked as decorative, so screen-reader users cannot understand its purpose.
issues.suggestion: Add an accessible name if the icon is meaningful, or hide it if it is decorative.
issues.description_technical: The <svg> element lacks role="img", aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title, and is not hidden with aria-hidden="true", violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user may hear nothing or hear only 'group', with no indication of what the icon represents.
issues.why_technical: SVGs are not exposed to assistive technology as images by default. Without an accessible name or decorative hiding, the icon's meaning is lost. NVDA + Firefox: may announce 'clickable group' with no purpose.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add role="img" and aria-label="<purpose>" or use a <title> element referenced by aria-labelledby. If decorative, add aria-hidden="true" focusable="false".

issues.description: A video element in the main content area is present without a captions track, so deaf or hard-of-hearing users cannot access the audio content.
issues.suggestion: Add a captions track to the video.
issues.description_technical: The <video> element lacks a <track kind="captions"> or kind="subtitles" element, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.2.2 (Captions Prerecorded).
issues.why_simple: A user who cannot hear the video's audio has no way to know what is being said.
issues.why_technical: Without a captions track, assistive technology cannot render synchronized text alternatives for the video's audio content. Screen-reader users with hearing loss cannot access the audio content visually.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add <track kind="captions" src="<captions.vtt>" srclang="en" label="English" default> inside the <video> element.

issues.description: A video element in the main content area lacks an audio description track or media alternative for visual-only information.
issues.suggestion: Add an audio description track or a text description of visual content.
issues.description_technical: The <video> element lacks a <track kind="descriptions"> or an aria-describedby reference to a text description, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.2.3 (Audio Description or Media Alternative Prerecorded).
issues.why_simple: A blind user cannot perceive important visual information shown in the video.
issues.why_technical: Without an audio description track or text alternative, assistive technology cannot convey visual content that is not described in the audio track. VoiceOver macOS: plays video audio but cannot describe visual-only information.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add <track kind="descriptions" src="<descriptions.vtt>" srclang="en" label="English"> inside the <video> element, or provide a text description linked via aria-describedby.

issues.description: A video element in the main content area may play audio automatically, and no visible pause/stop/mute control is present in the provided markup.
issues.suggestion: Ensure users can pause, stop, or mute any auto-playing audio, or avoid autoplay.
issues.description_technical: The <video> element may autoplay audio without a visible control, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.2 (Audio Control).
issues.why_simple: A user who cannot hear or who uses a screen reader may be disrupted by unexpected auto-playing audio.
issues.why_technical: Auto-playing audio can interfere with screen-reader output and lacks a mechanism to pause, stop, or mute it within the first 3 seconds. Screen-reader users may have difficulty locating hidden controls.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add visible controls to the <video> element (controls attribute) and avoid autoplay; if autoplay is required, provide an easily reachable mute/pause button.

issues.description: The main page heading 'Destination Mars' uses very light text color (#eee) without a visible dark background, likely failing contrast requirements.
issues.suggestion: Use a darker text color or ensure the background is dark enough to provide sufficient contrast.
issues.description_technical: The inline style color:#eee on the <h1> likely results in insufficient contrast against the background, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum).
issues.why_simple: Users with low vision or color vision deficiencies may not be able to read the heading.
issues.why_technical: Light gray (#eee) text on a light or default background typically falls below the 4.5:1 contrast ratio required for normal text. VoiceOver users with low vision may not see the main heading at all.
issues.suggestion_technical: Verify contrast with a contrast checker; adjust color to achieve at least 4.5:1 for normal text, e.g., use a darker foreground or a darker background.

issues.element: A trip to Mars starts in your imagination...
issues.description: The subheading 'A trip to Mars starts in your imagination...' uses a light blue-gray color (#acbad0) that likely fails contrast against the page background.
issues.suggestion: Use a darker or more saturated text color that provides sufficient contrast.
issues.description_technical: The inline style color:#acbad0 on the <h2> likely results in insufficient contrast against the background, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum).
issues.why_simple: Users with low vision may struggle to read the subheading text.
issues.why_technical: The color #acbad0 against a typical light background is likely below the 4.5:1 contrast ratio required for normal text. Users with low vision may miss this introductory subheading.
issues.suggestion_technical: Verify contrast with a contrast checker and adjust the color to achieve at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

issues.description: A malformed opening tag in the search region with an invalid attribute may break the form structure and confuse assistive technology.
issues.suggestion: Fix the malformed HTML so the form container is valid.
issues.description_technical: The <div <form="" ...> syntax is invalid HTML and may cause parsing errors, affecting WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships).
issues.why_simple: Screen readers and browsers may not correctly interpret the form region, making it harder to navigate.
issues.why_technical: Invalid HTML can cause assistive technology to miss the form's semantic structure and relationships between labels and controls. NVDA + Firefox: may fail to recognize the search landmark or form region.
issues.suggestion_technical: Replace <div <form="" class="span2-5 vap-col left-first" id="search"> with a valid container such as <div class="span2-5 vap-col left-first" id="search"> or <form class="span2-5 vap-col left-first" id="search">.

issues.element: <label class="country-pref-check"><input class="no-border" id="id-country-preference" name="country-preference" type="checkbox" value="1"/></label>
issues.description: A checkbox in the country preference area is wrapped in a label but contains no visible text, so the label's purpose may be unclear.
issues.suggestion: Add descriptive text inside the label or use aria-label/aria-labelledby.
issues.description_technical: The <label> element wrapping the checkbox contains no text content, which may result in an empty or unclear accessible name, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user may not understand what the checkbox does.
issues.why_technical: The accessible name for the checkbox is derived from the label text; an empty label provides no name to assistive technology. JAWS 2024: announces 'checkbox not checked' with no label context.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add visible text inside the <label>, e.g., <label class="country-pref-check"><input ...> Set country preference</label>, or add aria-label="Set country preference" to the input.

issues.description: A search input in the search region uses only a placeholder and has no visible or programmatic label.
issues.suggestion: Add a visible label or an accessible name for the search input.
issues.description_technical: The <input> element lacks an associated <label> or aria-label/aria-labelledby, relying solely on placeholder text, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions).
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user may not have a persistent label identifying the field, and placeholder text disappears once typing begins.
issues.why_technical: Placeholder text is not a substitute for a label; it is often not exposed consistently to assistive technology and disappears on input. NVDA + Chrome: may announce 'search edit blank' but the label is not persistent.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add <label for="search-query">Search</label> and id="search-query" to the input, or add aria-label="Search" to the input.

issues.description: A submit button in the search region has no visible text or accessible name.
issues.suggestion: Add a value or aria-label to the submit button.
issues.description_technical: The <input type="submit"> element lacks a value attribute or aria-label, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user may hear only 'submit' or 'button' without knowing what the button does.
issues.why_technical: The accessible name of a submit input is derived from its value attribute; without one, the button may have no meaningful name. VoiceOver iOS: announces 'submit button' with no action context.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add value="Search" or aria-label="Search" to the <input type="submit"> element.

issues.why_simple: Users may encounter unexpected behavior when activating the link.

issues.suggestion: Remove aria-level or add role="heading" and provide link text.

issues.why_simple: Screen-reader users may not understand the element's role or what the link does.
issues.why_technical: aria-level is ignored on elements without a heading role, and the empty link provides no accessible name or clear role. NVDA + Firefox: announces only 'link' with no name; VoiceOver iOS: cannot identify the destination when swiping through the video info section.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add visible text inside the <a> or use aria-label="Video title: <title>"; if aria-level is intended, use role="heading" and ensure the element is used appropriately.

issues.description_technical: The button's rendered dimensions are 6x16 pixels, which violates WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum) and may affect SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) by being difficult to perceive and activate.
issues.why_simple: Users with motor impairments or low vision may struggle to see or press the tiny button.
issues.why_technical: Very small interactive targets are hard to perceive and activate, especially for users with limited dexterity or vision. Voice Control: cannot reliably target a 6x16 px button by voice; Switch Access: the tiny hit area makes scanning and activation error-prone.

issues.suggestion_technical: Remove the <h2> if it is not needed, or add text content describing the video title.

issues.why_simple: Screen-reader users may encounter the same content multiple times or in an illogical order.
issues.why_technical: Duplicate content and invalid HTML can cause assistive technology to announce content in an order that does not match the visual layout. NVDA + Firefox: may announce repeated navigation blocks; TalkBack: swipe order can become unpredictable when DOM is malformed.
issues.suggestion_technical: Remove duplicate content where unintended and fix malformed tags to ensure the DOM order reflects the intended reading order.

issues.why_simple: Users who need to resize or restyle text cannot do so if the text is embedded in an image.
issues.why_technical: Text in images cannot be resized, reflowed, or read by some assistive technologies as effectively as real text.
issues.suggestion_technical: If the image contains text, recreate the content using HTML and CSS; if it is purely decorative, use alt="".

Several navigation links contain no visible text, so their purpose is impossible to determine from the link alone or from surrounding context.
issues.suggestion: Add descriptive text inside each empty link or provide an aria-label/aria-labelledby that describes the destination.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.4 requires the purpose of each link to be determinable from the link text alone or together with programmatically determined link context. Multiple <a class="link"> elements have empty text content and no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title attribute.
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user tabbing through links hears only "link" or the URL, with no clue where the link leads.
issues.why_technical: Assistive technologies expose the accessible name of these links as the href or nothing at all, failing the link-purpose requirement. NVDA + Firefox: Links List shows multiple 'https://dequeuniversity.com/...' entries; JAWS 2024: same unnamed links repeated; VoiceOver iOS: rotor link list is unusable.
issues.suggestion_technical: Why MarsCommuter

issues.description: A link in the main content/promotional area uses generic, non-descriptive text that does not clearly indicate its purpose or destination.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite the link text to describe the destination or action, e.g. "Learn about sending kids to Mars".
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.4 requires link text to describe the purpose of the link. The text "Send your kids to mars" is vague and duplicates nearby headings without clarifying the action (e.g., learn more, book, read details).
issues.why_simple: Users scanning links or hearing a list of links cannot tell what will happen if they activate this link.
issues.why_technical: Screen-reader users often pull up a list of links; non-descriptive text makes navigation inefficient and ambiguous. NVDA + Firefox: Links List shows 'Send your kids to mars' without context; JAWS 2024: same ambiguity in the links list.
issues.suggestion_technical: Learn about sending kids to Mars

issues.description: An empty heading in the fullscreen video player top controls provides no descriptive information about the section it introduces.
issues.suggestion: Remove the empty heading if it is decorative, or populate it with descriptive text about the video/player section.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 requires headings to describe the topic or purpose. The <h2> element has no text content and no aria-label/aria-labelledby, making it an empty heading in the outline.
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user navigating by headings encounters a blank heading and cannot understand the structure of the page.
issues.why_technical: Empty headings create noise in the heading hierarchy and do not help users navigate or understand content structure. NVDA + Firefox: announces 'heading level 2' with no content; JAWS 2024: includes a blank entry in the Headings List.
issues.suggestion_technical: Video: Life was possible on Mars

issues.element: <button aria-label="Close" class="ytSpecButtonShapeNextHost ..." title=""><div aria-hidden="true" class="ytSpecButtonShapeNextIcon"><c3-icon ...><span class="yt-icon-shape ytSpecIconShapeHost"><div aria-label="Share" ...>
issues.description: A button in the video player/share overlay area is labeled "Close" but appears to contain an icon whose visible label is "Share", creating a mismatch between visible text and accessible name.
issues.suggestion: Make the accessible name match the visible icon/text. If the button is for sharing, use aria-label="Share" or include "Share" in the label.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.3 requires the accessible name to contain the text that is presented visually. The button has aria-label="Close" while an inner element has aria-label="Share", and the visible icon likely represents Share. The accessible name does not match the visible label.
issues.why_simple: A speech-input user saying "Share" cannot activate the button because the accessible name is "Close", and a screen-reader user may be confused by the mismatch.
issues.why_technical: Speech recognition users rely on visible labels matching accessible names. When they differ, voice commands fail and screen-reader users receive inconsistent information. Voice Control iOS: saying 'Tap Share' fails because the accessible name is 'Close'; NVDA + Firefox: announces 'Close button' while the visible icon suggests Share.
issues.suggestion_technical: <button aria-label="Share" ...>...</button>

issues.description: A button in the video player controls area is only 16 by 6 CSS pixels and has no adjacent spacing, making it far smaller than the minimum target size.
issues.suggestion: Increase the button size to at least 24x24 CSS pixels or add sufficient spacing so the 24x24 target area does not overlap another target.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires targets to be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, unless they are inline, equivalent, or spaced. This button is 16x6 px with 0 px spacing, failing the minimum target size requirement.
issues.why_simple: Users with motor impairments who have difficulty aiming precisely cannot reliably tap or click this tiny control.
issues.why_technical: Small targets increase the probability of missing the control or activating a neighboring control, especially for users with tremors or limited dexterity. Voice Control: cannot reliably target a 6x16 px button by voice; Switch Access: the tiny hit area makes scanning and activation error-prone; TalkBack: touch exploration may miss the button entirely.
issues.suggestion_technical: Set min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px; on the button, or increase padding to achieve a 24x24 clickable area.

issues.description: A channel avatar button in the video info area is only 22 CSS pixels tall with zero spacing, which is below the 24x24 minimum target size.
issues.suggestion: Increase the button height to at least 24 px and ensure at least 24 px of non-overlapping target space around it.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires targets to be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless an exception applies. The rendered height is 22 px and data-closest-spacing is 0, so the 24x24 minimum target area is not met.
issues.why_simple: Users with motor impairments may struggle to activate the channel avatar link without accidentally hitting adjacent controls.
issues.why_technical: The 22 px height and zero spacing mean the minimum 24x24 target area overlaps or is smaller than required, increasing activation errors. TalkBack: touch exploration may activate adjacent video info controls; Switch Access: adjacent targets with no spacing are hard to distinguish.
issues.suggestion_technical: Set min-height: 24px; and add margin or padding so data-closest-spacing is at least 24 px.

issues.description: A hidden accessibility button in the video player controls may suppress or remove the default focus indicator, making keyboard focus invisible.
issues.suggestion: Ensure the button has a visible focus indicator when focused via keyboard, or remove it from the tab order if it is not meant to be interactive.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 requires a visible focus indicator. The class name "ytmA11yStylesHiddenButton" and the very small rendered size (16x6) suggest this control is visually hidden or styled without a visible focus ring. Without inspecting CSS, this is a plausible indicator removal.
issues.why_simple: A keyboard user tabbing to this control may not see where focus is, causing them to lose their place on the page.
issues.why_technical: If the control is visually hidden or uses outline:none without a :focus-visible replacement, assistive-technology users relying on sighted keyboard navigation cannot determine focus location. NVDA + Firefox: if the button remains focusable, it may be announced without a visible focus ring, leaving sighted keyboard users disoriented.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid; } or make the button visible and focusable with a clear focus ring.

issues.element: <div id="search"> containing nested forms and inputs
issues.description: The search region in the page header contains duplicate search inputs and forms with malformed markup, which may cause an illogical tab order.
issues.suggestion: Consolidate to a single search form, remove inputs outside the form, and ensure the DOM order matches the visual order.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 requires focusable components to receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability. The markup shows inputs outside a form, a <div <form=""> construct, and duplicate search fields, suggesting the DOM order may not match the visual order.
issues.why_simple: A keyboard user may tab through search fields in an unexpected sequence, making it confusing to use the search feature.
issues.why_technical: Malformed nesting and duplicate controls can cause browsers and assistive technologies to expose focusable elements in an order that does not match the visual layout. JAWS 2024: duplicate search inputs may be announced redundantly in Forms Mode, forcing users to guess which field is active.
issues.suggestion_technical: <form id="search"><input class="search" name="query" placeholder="search" type="text"/><input class="control-search" type="submit"/></form>

issues.description: Search inputs in the header search form have only a placeholder attribute and no persistent accessible label.
issues.suggestion: Add a visible <label> or an aria-label that describes the input as "Search".
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 requires labels to describe the topic or purpose. Placeholders are not persistent labels and often disappear once the user types. These inputs lack <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user or user with cognitive disabilities may not know what the field is for once the placeholder text disappears.
issues.why_technical: Placeholder text is not a robust accessible name and is often not exposed consistently to assistive technologies; it also disappears on input, removing context. NVDA: placeholder text may not be announced when the field is empty, leaving the input unnamed.
issues.suggestion_technical: <label for="search-query">Search</label><input id="search-query" class="search" name="query" type="text"/> or <input class="search" name="query" type="text" aria-label="Search"/>

issues.description: Search submit buttons in the header search form have no visible text or accessible label to indicate their purpose.
issues.suggestion: Add a value attribute or aria-label describing the button as "Search" or "Submit search".
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 requires labels to describe the topic or purpose. The submit inputs have no value attribute, no aria-label, and no visible text, so their purpose is not programmatically determinable.
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user hears only "button" or "submit" without knowing it triggers a search.
issues.why_technical: The accessible name of an <input type="submit"> without a value attribute defaults to browser-specific text (often "Submit" or "Submit Query"), which does not convey the search purpose. VoiceOver macOS: may announce only "submit button" with no search context.
issues.suggestion_technical: <input class="control-search" type="submit" value="Search"/> or <input class="control-search" type="submit" aria-label="Search"/>

issues.description: A country-preference checkbox has no visible or programmatic label, so users cannot understand what it controls.
issues.suggestion: Add descriptive text inside the <label> or use aria-label/aria-labelledby to name the checkbox.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 requires labels to describe the topic or purpose. The country-preference checkbox has no associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby, and is wrapped in an empty <label class="country-pref-check"> element.
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user hears only "checkbox, not checked" with no indication of what preference is being set.
issues.why_technical: Without an accessible name, assistive technologies cannot convey the purpose of the checkbox to users. TalkBack: swipe navigation will announce only "checkbox, not checked" with no hint about country preference.
issues.suggestion_technical: <label class="country-pref-check"><input class="no-border" id="id-country-preference" name="country-preference" type="checkbox" value="1"/> Remember my country preference</label>

issues.description: The page has multiple section headings but no corresponding landmark regions (main, nav, aside, etc.) to help users bypass repeated blocks.
issues.suggestion: Wrap the primary content in <main>, navigation in <nav>, and sidebar/footer content in <aside>/<footer> with descriptive labels.
issues.description_technical: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.1 can be satisfied by skip links or by proper landmark regions. While headings help, the absence of <main>, <nav>, and other landmarks means there is no programmatic bypass mechanism for repeated content.
issues.why_simple: A screen-reader user cannot jump directly to the main content or navigation regions using landmark shortcuts.
issues.why_technical: Landmark regions are exposed to assistive technologies as navigable page regions; without them, users must traverse all content linearly. JAWS 2024: pressing R to cycle regions will find no main or navigation landmarks, forcing linear navigation through the entire page.
issues.suggestion_technical: <nav aria-label="Primary">...</nav><main id="main">...</main><footer>...</footer>

issues.description: This 1x1 tracking image in the page body has no alt attribute, but it is purely decorative and should be hidden from assistive technology.
issues.suggestion: Add an empty alt attribute to the tracking pixel so it is ignored by assistive technology.
issues.description_technical: The element lacks an alt attribute. However, as a 1x1 tracking pixel, it conveys no information and should use alt="" to be treated as decorative.
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user would otherwise hear the filename or be distracted by a meaningless image announcement.
issues.why_technical: Section 508 requires a text equivalent for non-text elements, but decorative images can be hidden with alt="". Without it, NVDA may announce the image filename or "graphic" unnecessarily.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="" to the tracking pixel.

issues.description: This promotional image in the main content area has no alt attribute, so its content is invisible to screen reader users.
issues.suggestion: Add a short, meaningful description of the image content.
issues.description_technical: The element lacks an alt attribute, violating 36 CFR 1194.22(a) (mapped to WCAG SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A blind user cannot know what the image shows or what promotion it represents.
issues.why_technical: Section 508 requires a text equivalent for every non-text element; without alt text, assistive technology announces only the filename or nothing at all. NVDA + Chrome: will announce the long image URL or "graphic," providing no meaningful content.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="" to the element, or alt="" if purely decorative.

issues.description: The alt text for the space station image in the main content is a filename rather than a meaningful description of the image.
issues.suggestion: Replace the filename with a descriptive text equivalent.
issues.description_technical: The alt attribute contains a filename ('icecream.jpg ') that does not describe the image content, failing 36 CFR 1194.22(a) (mapped to WCAG SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user hears a filename and cannot understand what the image conveys.
issues.why_technical: Section 508 requires text equivalents to be meaningful; filenames do not serve as adequate text alternatives. VoiceOver iOS: will announce "icecream.jpg" without any indication the image shows a space station.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change alt="icecream.jpg " to alt="International space station orbiting Earth" or similar meaningful description.

issues.description: The alt text for the channel logo image in the video info section is generic and does not describe the image content or purpose.
issues.suggestion: Provide a descriptive alt text identifying the channel or image purpose.
issues.description_technical: The alt attribute 'thumbnail-image' is not descriptive of the channel logo image, failing 36 CFR 1194.22(a) (mapped to WCAG SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user cannot identify the channel or understand the image's purpose.
issues.why_technical: Section 508 requires text equivalents to convey the same information as the image; generic labels do not meet this requirement. JAWS 2024: will announce "thumbnail image graphic" without identifying the channel.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change alt="thumbnail-image" to alt="<Channel name> logo" or similar descriptive text.

issues.description: This SVG in the video player controls has no accessible name or role, so its purpose is unavailable to assistive technology.

issues.description_technical: The <svg> element lacks aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or role attributes, failing 36 CFR 1194.22(a) (mapped to WCAG SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content).

issues.why_technical: Section 508 requires a text equivalent for non-text content; SVGs without accessible names are ignored or announced generically by assistive technology. NVDA + Firefox: may skip the SVG entirely or announce "unknown" if referenced by a control.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add aria-label="<descriptive text>" and role="img" to the <svg>, or include a <title> element inside it.

issues.description: The video element in the main content area is hidden from assistive technology and has no visible caption or transcript alternative.
issues.suggestion: Provide captions and ensure the video is reachable by assistive technology.
issues.description_technical: The <video> element uses aria-hidden and tabindex="-1" with no <track kind="captions"> or transcript link, failing 36 CFR 1194.22(b) (mapped to WCAG SC 1.2.2 Captions).
issues.why_simple: Deaf or hard-of-hearing users cannot access the video's audio content.
issues.why_technical: Section 508 requires synchronized equivalent alternatives for multimedia; hiding the video from AT and omitting captions removes access entirely. TalkBack: the video is unreachable via swipe navigation because aria-hidden removes it from the accessibility tree.
issues.suggestion_technical: Remove aria-hidden and tabindex="-1", add <track kind="captions" src="..." srclang="en" label="English">, and provide a transcript link.
